key_insight: A monolithic ultralow-loss Si3N4 photonic chip can integrate photon-pair generation, qubit fusion, and state analysis to overcome loss-limited scaling in discrete-variable quantum processing.
engineering_relevance: This work advances manufacturable, CMOS-compatible quantum photonics by demonstrating a practical platform for higher-rate, larger-scale on-chip quantum circuits.
method: Integrated narrowband photon-pair sources on Si3N4
Built low-loss qubit-fusion circuits for combining EPR pairs
Used reconfigurable interferometers for on-chip state analysis
evidence_signal: The platform produced EPR states with fidelity 0.9875(3), heralded HOM visibility of 0.990(6), and four-photon GHZ states with fidelity 0.943(8) at a 27 Hz fourfold count rate.
watch_item: Despite strong performance, scaling still depends on maintaining ultralow loss and tight device uniformity as circuit depth and source count increase.
paper_title: An ultralow-loss integrated photonic platform for discrete-variable quantum information processing
